questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and Correcting Statements

subQuestions.questionText:
The marketing channel where livestock is sold to the highest bidder:
A. Farm gate
B. Auction
C. Direct marketing
D. Indirect marketing
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Auction (2 marks)
At an auction the animals are sold to whoever offers the highest bid.

subQuestions.questionText:
The phase in the entrepreneurial process where a farmer secures capital for infrastructure and equipment:
A. Starting an enterprise
B. Resource mobilisation
C. Identification of an opportunity
D. Planning
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Resource mobilisation (2 marks)
Resource mobilisation is the phase in which the entrepreneur gathers the money, land, equipment and people needed to start the business.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following is NOT a problem encountered when drawing up a business plan:
A. Plan is vague with loop holes
B. Unrealistic assumptions and projections
C. Business is financially very strong
D. Hiding weaknesses and risks
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Business is financially very strong (2 marks)
Being financially strong is an advantage, not a problem. The other options are all pitfalls when writing a business plan.

options.A: Plan is vague with loop holes

subQuestions.questionText:
When a price is fixed in a market, …
(i) the price set for the goods and services allows bargaining.
(ii) the price is held constant regardless of the cost of production.
(iii) the price is maintained at a given level by controlling supply and demand.
(iv) there is an agreement between the participants to buy and sell at a predetermined price.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (i), (ii) and (iv)
B. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (iii) and (iv)
D. (i), (ii) and (iii)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - (ii), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
A fixed price does not allow bargaining, so statement (i) is false. Fixed prices are kept constant, maintained by controlling supply and demand, and set by agreement between participants.

subQuestions.questionText:
The management strategies that allow a farmer to manage risks:
A. Diversification and risk sharing
B. Risk sharing and problem solving
C. Diversification and organising
D. Specialisation and planning
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Diversification and risk sharing (2 marks)
Spreading production over several enterprises (diversification) and sharing risk (co-operatives, insurance, contracts) are the two main risk-management strategies.

subQuestions.questionText:
… is/are a cause of labour shortages on farms.
A. Fair labour practices
B. The provision of medical insurance and pension
C. Less attractive working conditions
D. The provision of incentives
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Less attractive working conditions (2 marks)
Poor or less attractive working conditions drive workers away from farms, causing labour shortages. The other options help to attract and retain workers.

options.B: The provision of medical insurance and pension

subQuestions.questionText:
The following description implies that land is indestructible:
A. Has different production potentials
B. Found in a specific environment
C. Cannot produce anything by itself
D. Can renew itself after it has been degraded
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Can renew itself after it has been degraded (2 marks)
Land being able to recover after degradation shows that it cannot be permanently destroyed, i.e. it is indestructible.

options.D: Can renew itself after it has been degraded

subQuestions.questionText:
The following are problems related to capital as a production factor:
(i) Scarcity
(ii) Low risk
(iii) Undercapitalisation
(iv) High interest rates
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (i), (ii) and (iv)
B. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (iii) and (iv)
D. (i), (ii) and (iii)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - (i), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
Scarcity of capital, undercapitalisation and high interest rates are all capital problems. 'Low risk' (ii) is not a problem.

subQuestions.questionText:
When the alleles on homologous chromosomes differ, an organism is …
A. heterozygous.
B. recessive.
C. dominant.
D. homozygous.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - heterozygous (2 marks)
Heterozygous means the two alleles for a gene (one on each homologous chromosome) are different.

subQuestions.questionText:
… is a measure of how much better or less than average the offspring of an individual will be for a particular characteristic.
A. Breeding system
B. Pedigree performance
C. Breeding method
D. Estimated breeding value
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Estimated breeding value (2 marks)
The estimated breeding value (EBV) predicts the genetic merit an animal will pass to its offspring, expressed as a deviation from the average.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The response of demand or supply to a change in the price of a product.
COLUMN B options: A. sustainable marketing  B. communication skills  C. grant  D. heredity  E. progeny  F. price elasticity  G. multisegmented marketing  H. price inelasticity  I. loan  J. analytical skills
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: F - price elasticity (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Use of recyclable material when packaging produce.
COLUMN B options: A. sustainable marketing  B. communication skills  C. grant  D. heredity  E. progeny  F. price elasticity  G. multisegmented marketing  H. price inelasticity  I. loan  J. analytical skills
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A - sustainable marketing (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Funding provided by the state that does not have to be paid back.
COLUMN B options: A. sustainable marketing  B. communication skills  C. grant  D. heredity  E. progeny  F. price elasticity  G. multisegmented marketing  H. price inelasticity  I. loan  J. analytical skills
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C - grant (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The ability of a farm manager to forecast future demand, prices and trends.
COLUMN B options: A. sustainable marketing  B. communication skills  C. grant  D. heredity  E. progeny  F. price elasticity  G. multisegmented marketing  H. price inelasticity  I. loan  J. analytical skills
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: J - analytical skills (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The transfer of characteristics from parents to offspring.
COLUMN B options: A. sustainable marketing  B. communication skills  C. grant  D. heredity  E. progeny  F. price elasticity  G. multisegmented marketing  H. price inelasticity  I. loan  J. analytical skills
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D - heredity (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The process of collecting, recording, analysing and interpreting data on consumers, competitors and the environment for a product.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Market research (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A financial document that summarises assets and liabilities.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Balance sheet (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A type of cell division that leads to the production of haploid sex cells.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Meiosis (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The selection of organisms that is driven by the particular traits a breeder desires.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Artificial selection (also accepted: mass / pedigree / family / progeny selection) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The technology that involves highly advanced scientific techniques of altering the genes to obtain a desired characteristic.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Genetic modification (also accepted: genetic manipulation / genetic engineering / GM) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the underlined word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
A retailer is the type of buyer who works for commission on behalf of other participants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Broker (also accepted: agent / intermediary) (1 mark)
A broker buys and sells on behalf of others for a commission. A retailer buys goods to resell directly to consumers.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the underlined word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Variable costs do not change with the level of production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Fixed (costs) (1 mark)
Fixed costs stay the same regardless of production level; variable costs change with production.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the underlined word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Biolistic is a technique where bacteria are used to incorporate genes of a desired plant into the DNA of another organism.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Bacterial carrier (Agrobacterium tumefaciens) (1 mark)
Using bacteria to carry genes into a plant is the bacterial-carrier method. Biolistics ('gene gun') uses metal particles coated with DNA.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the underlined word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Genetics is a measure where the genes contribute to the phenotype.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Heritability (1 mark)
Heritability measures the proportion of the phenotype that is due to genes. Genetics is the study of heredity as a whole.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the underlined word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Incomplete dominance is a pattern of inheritance where characteristics of both parents are expressed in the phenotype of an offspring.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Co-dominance (1 mark)
Co-dominance is when both parental characteristics are fully and separately expressed. In incomplete dominance the offspring shows a blended, intermediate phenotype.

questions.title: Section B, Question 2: Agricultural Management and Marketing

subQuestions.questionText:
A diagram in the question paper shows three agricultural marketing systems:
A – Members working together voluntarily to reach a common goal.
B – Farmers can sell when and where they want at the highest possible price.
C – Government decides on prices of agricultural products, such as wheat, in order to stabilise the prices.
Identify agricultural marketing systems A, B and C represented in the diagram.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Co-operative marketing (1 mark)
B - Free marketing (1 mark)
C - Controlled marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO principles of marketing system A (co-operative marketing).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Voluntary and open membership
• Democratic member control
• Equal economic participation and contribution
• Autonomy and independence
• Provision of education, training and information to members
• Concern for the sustainable development of communities
• A single vote to each member / all members are shareholders
• Marketing is based on a pool system
• Co-operation among co-operatives
• Only members may deliver products and benefit
• Members are paid on a commission basis
• Members receive a small interest on their share capital
• Products of members are standardised

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE disadvantage of marketing system B (free marketing).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Too much competition
• Producers may collude (form cartels) to fix prices
• Greater fluctuations in prices
• Marketing costs are too high
• Producers are responsible for marketing the product themselves
• Limited bargaining power
• High risk / financial losses
• Farmers may lack the necessary marketing skills
• Exploitation by consumers

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE benefit of marketing system A (co-operative marketing) to the members.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Better bargaining power than individual farmers
• Economies of scale through the pooling system
• Access to professional expertise / better infrastructure
• Elimination of intermediaries
• Bulk purchasing of inputs at better prices
• Access to government funding programmes for co-operatives
• Risk is shared by all members
• Credit is extended to members
• More stable prices / dividends are paid
• The producer has more time for farming instead of marketing

subQuestions.questionText:
A graph in the question paper shows price on the y-axis and quantity on the x-axis. Curve A slopes downward from top-left to bottom-right; curve B slopes upward from bottom-left to top-right; the two curves cross at point C. Point D lies above C (price higher than equilibrium) and point E lies below C (price lower than equilibrium).
Identify curves A and B in the graph.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Demand (curve) (1 mark)
B - Supply (curve) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the economic term for point C (where the demand and supply curves cross).
subQuestions.memoText: Market equilibrium (equilibrium point). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the situation at the market illustrated by D (price above equilibrium) and E (price below equilibrium).
subQuestions.memoText:
D - Surplus (supply exceeds demand) (1 mark)
E - Shortage (demand exceeds supply) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the relationship between the price and curves A (demand) and B (supply) indicated in the graph.
subQuestions.memoText: The higher the price, the higher the quantity supplied (curve B) and the lower the quantity demanded (curve A); the lower the price, the lower the quantity supplied and the higher the quantity demanded. Price and supply are directly related; price and demand are inversely related. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
The legislative and regulatory framework controls the marketing of agricultural products and is intended to protect both producers and consumers.
State TWO roles of legislation for the effective marketing of agricultural products.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Promotes a fair, accessible and sustainable marketplace
• Prevents unfair marketing and business practices
• Ensures product information is given in simple language
• Enhances the viability of the agricultural sector / increases market access
• Authorises the establishment of regulations for marketing agricultural products
• Controls the sale of certain agricultural products
• Ensures products comply with set standards (produce and packaging)
• Sets and maintains national standards at processing sites
• Promotes agricultural product safety
• Regulates market agents and improves their functioning

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that hamper the marketing of agricultural products.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Perishability / spoilage
• Seasonal fluctuation in production
• Lack of control over production
• Wide distribution of production areas / high transport costs
• Bulkiness / low value in relation to volume
• Intermediaries / agents
• Poor or insufficient infrastructure
• Risks / accidents / theft / strikes
• Lack of capital
• Variation in the quality (standardisation) of products

subQuestions.questionText:
A picture in the question paper illustrates a function of agricultural marketing (produce being turned into a packaged, manufactured product in a factory).
Identify the agricultural marketing function depicted in the picture.
subQuestions.memoText: Processing / value adding (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of the marketing function identified in QUESTION 2.4.1 (processing / value adding).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Avoids oversupply / spoilage / reduces wastage of excess produce
• Improves food safety
• Increases shelf life
• Provides job opportunities
• Enables easy packaging / handling
• Ensures food security / availability all year round
• Adds value to the product
• Product can be transported over longer distances
• Increases the demand for the product
• Increases profitability / revenue

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO other main agricultural marketing functions NOT shown in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): transportation; storage; packaging. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
It is important for entrepreneurs to have good qualities to be able to run a business successfully.
Distinguish between an entrepreneur and entrepreneurship.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Entrepreneur: a person who exercises initiative by taking advantage of a business opportunity. (1 mark)
• Entrepreneurship: the process of discovering, evaluating and exploiting new business opportunities. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the success factor (Appreciation; Punctuality; Leadership; Motivation; Confidence) that matches the statement:
(a) The entrepreneur sets standards and executes the roles for the success of the business.
subQuestions.memoText: Leadership (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the success factor (Appreciation; Punctuality; Leadership; Motivation; Confidence) that matches the statement:
(b) The entrepreneur is on time for duty on a daily basis.
subQuestions.memoText: Punctuality (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the component of the SWOT analysis represented by the statement:
Increased competition from other producers.
subQuestions.memoText: Threat (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the component of the SWOT analysis represented by the statement:
Having out-dated and inefficient machinery.
subQuestions.memoText: Weakness (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the component of the SWOT analysis represented by the statement:
Skilled workforce.
subQuestions.memoText: Strength (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the component of the SWOT analysis represented by the statement:
Newly introduced technology that increases farm efficiency is coming soon.
subQuestions.memoText: Opportunity (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
A business plan is a document that describes a business that a farmer wants to start, its goals and objectives.
Name TWO components that should be included in a good business plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Title page
• Table of contents / index
• An executive business profile / general overview of the business
• A marketing plan
• A production / operational plan
• A human resource plan
• A financial plan
• A SWOT analysis
• Supporting documentation

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason for drawing up a business plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• To determine the financial needs of the business
• To test the feasibility / economic viability of the business
• To secure funding / attract investors or partners
• To ensure effective business management
• To reposition the business
• To foresee problems
• To gain knowledge about market opportunities / competitors
• To guide daily operations / provide time frames
• To outline the roles and responsibilities of those involved
• To map out objectives or goals
• To provide guidelines for decision making

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the amount of fertiliser applied and the quantity of maize produced on a piece of land.
Fertilisers (kg) | Maize (bags)
5  | 10
10 | 25
15 | 35
20 | 40
25 | 40
Draw a line graph using the information in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Line graph. Marking rubric (1 mark each):
• Correct heading
• X-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Fertiliser applied, kg)
• Y-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Maize production, bags)
• Correct units (kg and bags)
• Line graph drawn
• Accuracy (80%+ correctly plotted); the line rises steeply at first, then flattens between 20 kg and 25 kg (both at 40 bags)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the economic characteristic of the land depicted in the table above (where extra fertiliser eventually produces no extra maize).
subQuestions.memoText: Land is subject to the law of diminishing returns. (1 mark)
subQuestions.topic: Production Factors - Law of Diminishing Returns

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the function of the land reflected in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): land provides food; land provides space (for production).

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO methods of increasing the productivity of the land other than the one in the table (fertiliser).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Use of scientific methods / technology / precision farming
• Improving water management (irrigation)
• Changing cropping practices / intercropping / crop rotation
• Restoring land potential / avoiding erosion
• Farming the land more efficiently / consolidating small uneconomical land units

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Different types of labour are employed in a sheep production enterprise: Seasonal, Permanent, Casual.
Identify the type of labour employed to perform the task: feeding stud rams.
subQuestions.memoText: Permanent (1 mark) — daily feeding is an ongoing task requiring permanent staff.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of labour (Seasonal, Permanent, Casual) employed to perform the task: shearing sheep.
subQuestions.memoText: Seasonal (1 mark) — shearing is done at a particular time of the year.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of labour (Seasonal, Permanent, Casual) employed to perform the task: installation of water troughs on the farm.
subQuestions.memoText: Casual (1 mark) — a once-off short task.

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO ways in which the farmer can improve the living conditions of farm labourers in this farming enterprise.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Better housing that is safe and secure / proper sanitation
• Supply of water / food / electricity
• Recreational facilities to relax and socialise

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Conditions of employment of farm workers are listed as:
A – Entitlement to tea, lunch breaks and leaves of absence
B – Affiliation rights to labour unions
C – Provision of protective gear when working with hazardous chemicals
D – Compensation for injuries while on duty
Identify the letter (A–D) of the condition addressed by the Labour Relations Act, 1995 (Act 66 of 1995).
subQuestions.memoText: B (affiliation rights to labour unions). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the letter (A–D) of the condition addressed by the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993).
subQuestions.memoText: C (provision of protective gear when working with hazardous chemicals). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the letter (A–D) of the condition addressed by the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1997 (Act 75 of 1997).
subQuestions.memoText: A (entitlement to tea, lunch breaks and leaves of absence). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the legal document that needs to be signed between the farmer and the farm worker on employment.
subQuestions.memoText: A labour (employment) contract. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
A diagram in the question paper shows examples of different types of capital commonly used in farming, labelled A, B and C (A shows a tractor and vehicles; B shows land, a farmhouse and fixed structures; C shows seed, fertiliser, fuel and feed).
Identify the type of capital represented by A, B and C in the diagram.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Movable capital (1 mark)
B - Fixed capital (1 mark)
C - Working / floating / production capital (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO methods of creating capital.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): savings; production (reinvesting profits); credit / loan; inheritance; grants / donations.

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below represents a financial record for the third quarter of a farming enterprise.
Item | October (R) | November (R) | December (R)
Opening balance | 500 | 10 150 | 13 538
Income – Livestock sales | 3 500 | 3 500 | 2 000
Income – Sales from crops | 4 300 | 0 | 0
Income – Capital | 5 500 | 4 500 | 2 200
Total income (receipts) | 13 300 | 8 000 | 4 200
Expenses – Transport | 2 800 | 3 700 | 4 600
Expenses – Interest on amount owed | 350 | 412 | 674
Expenses – Wages for labourers | 500 | 500 | 3 500
Total expenses (payments) | 3 650 | 4 612 | 8 774
Profit/Loss | 9 650 | 3 388 | A
Closing balance | B | 13 538 | ?
Identify the financial record in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText: Cash flow statement (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason for the answer to QUESTION 3.5.1 by referring to the table.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): it shows all income and expenditure for a specific period / income (receipts) / expenditure (payments) / opening and closing balances for each month / profit or loss for each month / cash items only.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the profit or loss for December represented by A in the table above. Include the formula and show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Profit/Loss = Total income − Total expenditure
= R4 200 − R8 774
= −R4 574 (a loss of R4 574) (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the closing balance represented by B in the table above (October). Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Closing balance = Opening balance + Profit/Loss
= R500 + R9 650
= R10 150 (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 3.6.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Management is the effective combination and co-ordination of human, physical and financial resources to maximise profit.
Indicate the management principle applicable to the statement: the manager puts different planned activities into action.
subQuestions.memoText: Implementation (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.6.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the management principle applicable to the statement: development of short- and long-term strategies based on available resources.
subQuestions.memoText: Planning (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.6.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE example of an internal force influencing farming businesses.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): available resources; available management capacity and competencies; organisational structure; culture of the business; financial position of the farm; management systems available; products produced; investment in research and development; use of outdated equipment.

subQuestions.label: 3.6.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE example of an external force affecting farming businesses.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): economic forces; political forces; ethical forces; legal forces; socio-cultural forces / population demographics; education levels in the area; competition; technology; environmental forces / nature.

questions.title: Section B, Question 4: Basic Agricultural Genetics

subQuestions.questionText:
Mendel studied garden peas and concluded that there are two alleles for each characteristic, which separate from each other during gametogenesis to form the 'genetic makeup' of an individual.
Give a term for the underlined words ('genetic makeup') in the paragraph above.
subQuestions.memoText: Genotype (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce Mendel's Law of Inheritance illustrated in the paragraph above (two alleles separating from each other during gametogenesis).
subQuestions.memoText: Mendel's law of segregation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment.
subQuestions.memoText: Different pairs of genes (alleles) separate independently of the members of other pairs (1 mark) when two or more characteristics are inherited together (1 mark). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
In pigs, red hair colour (R) is dominant over white colour (r). A white sow was mated with a red boar and all piglets in the F1 were red.
Use the Punnett square method to determine the genotype of the F1-generation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Because all F1 piglets are red, the red boar must be homozygous RR. Cross: RR (boar) × rr (sow).
Male gametes: R, R. Female gametes: r, r.
Punnett square offspring: Rr, Rr, Rr, Rr.
Marking (1 mark each): correct gametes of male parent; correct gametes of female parent; correct genotype of offspring (Rr); Punnett square correctly populated with gametes and offspring.
F1 genotype = Rr (all heterozygous).

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of homozygous red piglets in the F1-generation (from the RR × rr cross).
subQuestions.memoText:
= 0/4 × 100
= 0% — every F1 piglet is heterozygous (Rr), so none is homozygous red. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Assume that four pairs of genes control the height of pepper plants. The base height of a recessive plant (aabbccdd) is 40 cm. Each additive (capital-letter) allele contributes 4 cm to the base height.
Calculate the height of a plant with an AaBbCcDD genotype.
subQuestions.memoText:
AaBbCcDD has 5 additive alleles (A, B, C, D, D).
Height = 40 cm + (5 × 4 cm)
= 40 cm + 20 cm
= 60 cm (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 4.3.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the genotype of a pepper plant with a height of 68 cm (base 40 cm, each additive allele = 4 cm, four gene pairs).
subQuestions.memoText:
68 cm − 40 cm = 28 cm → 28 ÷ 4 = 7 additive alleles (7 capital letters out of 8).
Any genotype with 7 dominant alleles, e.g. AABBCCDd / AABBCcDD / AABbCCDD / AaBBCCDD. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.3.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the phenotype of the shortest pepper plant.
subQuestions.memoText: 40 cm (genotype aabbccdd — no additive alleles). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Streaked hairlessness is a disorder that results in streaks of missing hairs in Holstein cattle. It is caused by a dominant allele located on the X-chromosome.
Indicate whether the characteristic explained above shows X-linked or Y-linked inheritance.
subQuestions.memoText: X-linked inheritance (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a term that refers to characteristics that are located on the X- and Y-chromosomes.
subQuestions.memoText: Sex-linked characteristics (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
A pedigree diagram in the question paper shows the inheritance of fleece length in sheep over three generations (individuals numbered 1–10). Long fleece is dominant (L) over short fleece (l); shaded symbols = long fleece, unshaded = short fleece; circles = female, squares = male. Individuals 1 (female) and 2 (male) are the founding parents.
From the data above, indicate a characteristic which is dominant.
subQuestions.memoText: Long fleece (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the genotype of individual 5 in the pedigree diagram (an unshaded / short-fleece individual).
subQuestions.memoText: ll (homozygous recessive) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the phenotype of individual 9 in the pedigree diagram (an unshaded symbol).
subQuestions.memoText: Short fleece (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether individual 8 in the pedigree diagram is homozygous or heterozygous (a shaded / long-fleece individual with a short-fleece offspring).
subQuestions.memoText: Heterozygous (Ll) — it has long fleece but produced a short-fleece offspring, so it must carry the recessive allele. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the number of female animals in the pedigree diagram that are homozygous recessive (short fleece).
subQuestions.memoText: Two (individuals 1 and 9). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Variation is the foundation for selection and breeding. Define the term variation.
subQuestions.memoText: Variation is the differences (1 mark) among individuals of the same species (1 mark). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO causes of variation.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Genetic / internal causes (mutation, meiosis / crossing-over, random fertilisation) (1 mark)
• Environmental / external causes (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE type of mutagen.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): biological; physical; chemical.

subQuestions.label: 4.7.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A schematic representation in the question paper shows different breeding systems in cattle.
Breeding system 1: Afrikaner (bull) × Hereford (cow) → F1-offspring.
Breeding system 2: repeated matings within a Holstein herd — Holstein bull 1 × Holstein cow 1 → Holstein heifer 1; Holstein bull 1 × Holstein heifer 2 → Holstein heifer 3; etc.
Identify the breeding system represented by Breeding system 1.
subQuestions.memoText: Crossbreeding (crossing two different breeds). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.7.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the breeding system represented by the crossing of Holstein (bull 1) with Holstein (heifer 2) in breeding system 2 (mating an animal back to a close relative within the same herd).
subQuestions.memoText: Line breeding (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: From the schematic representations above, identify the breeding system that promotes heterosis.
subQuestions.memoText: Crossbreeding (Breeding system 1). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO disadvantages of inbreeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Variation decreases
• Undesirable characteristics can be bred into the progeny
• Reduction in vitality
• Animals are less resistant to diseases
• Poorer adaptability to the environment
• Undesirable genes are made homozygous
• Inbreeding depression occurs
• Increases the expression of lethal genes / deformities
• Expensive

subQuestions.questionText:
Genetic modification is a technology used by plant and animal breeders to improve the performance of organisms.
State TWO health benefits of genetically modified crops.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Food low in pesticide residues / farmers use less pesticide
• Higher nutritional value
• Food with better flavour / colour / texture
• Production of medication

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO aims of genetic modification in animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Develop new vaccines and medication for animals / people
• Develop animal models to study animal / human diseases
• Increase the nutritional quality of animal products
• Increase the health quality of animal products
• Increase the yield of animal products
• Breed more fertile animals
• Improve production characteristics / growth rate / milk production
• Produce products for therapeutic use
• Improve resistance to pests / diseases / harsh environmental conditions
